AAPL.rationale: Apple presents a mixed but slightly positive picture. On the positive side, the company shows strong YoY growth (revenue +16.6%, EPS +21.8% in Q2 FY2026), excellent profitability (27.2% net margin, 47.9% gross margin), and a Services business growing to record levels with ~76% gross margins. The balance sheet is solid with improving equity ($106.5B vs $66.8B a year ago) and manageable debt. Market share is gaining across product categories, and the ecosystem with 90%+ iPhone retention provides durable competitive advantages. However, several headwinds temper enthusiasm: (1) Valuation is elevated at 38x P/E, near the upper end of its 30.5-43.1x 12-month range, and P/B of 43.7x is rich; (2) QoQ metrics show significant seasonal decline (revenue -22.7%, EPS -29.2%), which is normal for Apple's Q1-to-Q2 transition but still notable; (3) Rising memory costs are pressuring margins, with CEO Tim Cook calling cost increases 'unsustainable' and the company raising prices on Macs and iPads; (4) Regulatory headwinds from DOJ antitrust lawsuit and EU Digital Markets Act threaten the high-margin Services business; (5) The stock has rallied +22.1% in the past quarter, potentially pricing in much of the good news. The upcoming Q3 earnings on July 30 could serve as a near-term catalyst, with analysts expecting EPS of $1.88 (+19.8% YoY) and the company having beaten estimates in each of the last four quarters. However, the memory cost headwinds and recent price increases create execution risk. Overall, Apple's fundamental health is strong but the stock appears fairly-to-slightly-expensive versus its own history, with meaningful near-term risks from component costs and regulation that partially offset the positive trajectory.
